findings.title: suite-gpu will fail by construction on the TF32 canary
findings.argument: test_gpu_strided_canary carries @gpu (reason 'CUDA disabled for CPU lane') and a second skipif that skips whenever NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE is set. The staged line's env sets NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0 (dry_suite-gpu_*_R5D.json env), and pytest_line passes that env to the child. On the GPU line the canary therefore skips for the TF32 reason. The plugin marks a test GPU-gated by the presence of any skipif whose reason names CUDA, not by which condition fired, so it lists the canary in gpu_skips and the line returns False. BWD-R1 ran this canary on its own line with the override removed (scripts/bwd_r1_stage_r5.py:147). r5b's name-based rule had the same outcome. Shown on CPU: the canary is in gpu_marked and its skip is in gpu_skips (checks/f08_plugin_tf32_canary_markers.json). The GPU-line reason differs only in which condition fires.
findings.fix: Classify a skip as a GPU skip by the reason of the skip that fired (CUDA or fixture-absent), not by marker presence. Run the canary with NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE removed (as BWD-R1 did), or list it as an expected skip on this line.

findings.title: The digests run inside every checkpointed line, including G5's timed and measured window
findings.argument: Each segment now copies to host and sha256-hashes its activation, the style tensor and every parameter it consumes, in forward and again in replay (31 segments in fine mode), plus its output. G5's forward and backward seconds now include that work, so they are not comparable with r4's 2.2 s / 0.9 s. Any device-side contiguous copy taken for .numpy() would also fall inside the reserved-peak window. The bar is report-only, so this is a disclosure, not a defect.
findings.fix: Add a digest-off switch for the G5 lines, or report G5 timings as including digests.

findings.title: r5m02's kill rule needs the output digest to move as well as the input digest
findings.argument: The rule is: caught requires mismatched == edited AND input_mismatched == edited. The input digest of the edited segment changes by construction. If rounding absorbs the one-ulp edit before the output, the line would report r5m02 as surviving even though F07's input check caught it.
findings.fix: Score the kill on input_mismatched == edited, and report the output mismatch as information.

findings.title: The note says segment operations read no tensor outside their arguments
findings.argument: resblk1d reads self.C(p['div']) (Voice model.py:771), a cached constant tensor in model._consts reached through self, not passed as a checkpoint input. Harmless: frozen constants that are never written. The sentence is still not accurate.
findings.fix: Say that the only closure-reached tensors are the model's cached scalar constants (model.C), which are never written.
